doc.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Wynton Marsalis as mentor and the Mellon Jazz Festival workshops
summary: He met Wynton at 14-15 in a Philadelphia workshop and Wynton became a big-brother mentor; Mellon festival workshops brought Branford, Bobby Watson, Ron Carter and others.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well in the span of a few years you’ve been with some pretty good bands.

Let’s see. I first met Wynton Marsalis when I was fifteen years old, fourteen years old. He came to Philadelphia to do a workshop with the local Philadelphia high school students. And Wynton was like a mentor for all of the young high school students. However I was probably one of the only ones that had all of his albums and knew every song off of all of those albums. So I tried to impress him by playing a song off of the record. I can’t remember which one it was but I caught him. And from that point on he © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

became like my big brother. I mean he used to go so far as to call my teachers at school to make sure I was getting good grades. So Wynton was definitely someone that I needed. Wynton is someone that everyone needs in their life, especially when you’re that young you know, to have a mentor like that that takes you under their wing and just set you straight.
Keep you on the right track.

Exactly. And then after meeting Wynton I met his brother Branford and I met Bobby Watson. I had a chance to meet a lot of great musicians as they came through Philadelphia to do different workshops. There was an annual workshop that goes on, a jazz festival rather that goes on in Philadelphia every year, sponsored by Mellon Bank, the Mellon Jazz Festival. And every year before they have the big gala concert they have all of the players come and do workshops for the high school students. So I had a chance to meet and play with like Red Rodney and Kenny Barron, Curtis Fuller, Jimmy Heath, Walter Davis Jr., I first met Ron Carter with the Mellon Jazz Festival. So I mean that festival brought a lot of high school students who wanted to go, you know, in touch with these musicians. And that was fantastic you know. Because like I say you need that when you’re that young.
